subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] problem plotting recombination frequency by old scores when mapping

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] problem plotting recombination frequency by old scores when mapping
parts:
markerlrt() can't be used to estimate recombination fractions; it just performs a general likelihood ratio test for association between genotypes at two markers.

If you want to plot rf vs lod, you need to use the est.rf() function first.

karl


On Jun 28, 2013, at 9:52 AM, Jen <jen.s...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hello,
>
> I am in the process of trying to create a de novo linkage map for an F2 population containing a mix of dominant and codominant markers (coded as such in the cross object), and have run into a problem when I try to plot the recombination frequencies versus the LOD scores.
>
> I want to use the markerlrt() function to calculate recombination frequencies (since I know there is likely to be seg. distortion in the population), but I've also tried using est.rf(). After using either one of these functions, I try the following code to the plot the recombination fraction versus the LOD score:
>
> rf= pull.rf(cross, what="rf")
> lod= pull.rf(cross, what="lod")
> plot(as.numeric(rf), as.numeric(lod), xlab="recombination fraction", ylab="LOD")
>
> but the resulting plot is a straight line, with identical values one each access, as if the LOD score is being plotted versus the LOD score (I don't think the rf is being plotted vs the rf because the values range from 0 to 120), or as if the rf values == the LOD values. When I look at the rf values in the rf object, they look like they are in the right range (between 0 and 1), but when I look at the values in the 'lod' object, they do not appear to match those of either axis of my plot -- in fact, they appear identical to the rf values! I have no idea what's going on here... any insight would be much appreciated!
>
> Thanks very much!
> Jen
